scope: Williamson County community-level resources (ISDs, local nonprofits, WCCHD, LSCC, transit, libraries)

records.name: Round Rock Area Serving Center Food Pantry and Financial Assistance
records.description_en: Gives free groceries from a food pantry and can help with some bills through vouchers or checks. It also runs a thrift store and a home food delivery program.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people living in Round Rock and southern Williamson County.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Round Rock / southern Williamson County resident

records.how_to_apply: Create an account and submit a request online first; you must have a food voucher before visiting the pantry. Online requests are processed Monday-Thursday 10 AM-5 PM and Friday 10 AM-4 PM.
records.hours: Food pantry: Mon-Fri 10 AM-4 PM (last check-in 3:30 PM), Sat 9 AM-1 PM. Voucher/check pickup: Mon-Fri 10 AM-3:30 PM, Sat 9 AM-1 PM. Thrift store: Mon-Sat 10 AM-4 PM.
records.notes: The site says photo ID is not required for food help. Clients MUST apply online and have a food voucher before entering the pantry. Email: Hello@rrasc.org.

records.name: The Caring Place Food Pantry and Assistance Programs
records.description_en: Free food pantry plus help with bills, free laundry nights (Loads of Caring), thrift store vouchers, and holiday programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Georgetown, Andice, Bartlett, Florence, Granger, Jarrell, Jonah, Schwertner, Walburg, Weir, and parts of Hutto inside Georgetown ISD. Other rules apply to each program.
records.how_to_apply: Visit Programs & Services at 2001 Railroad Avenue (Mon-Fri 9 AM-4 PM) or call (512) 943-0700. The food pantry is at 2000 Railroad Avenue.
records.hours: Food pantry: Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri 9 AM-4 PM; Thu 2-6 PM. Programs & Services: Mon-Fri 9 AM-4 PM. Loads of Caring: 2nd Tuesday and last Thursday of each month, 4-8 PM.
records.notes: Programs & Services office is across the street at 2001 Railroad Avenue. Required documents for general help were not listed online - call ahead.

records.name: Senior Independence Program
records.description_en: Limited help with rent, mortgage, and utility bills for older adults, plus case management. Extra help is available for City of Georgetown utility bills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults age 65 and older in The Caring Place service area. Other eligibility guidelines apply.
documents_needed: Current signed lease or mortgage statement
Most recent utility bills
Social Security or retirement award letter
records.how_to_apply: Go to Programs & Services at 2001 Railroad Avenue, Georgetown (Mon-Fri 9 AM-4 PM) or call (512) 943-0700.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 9 AM-4 PM

records.name: Hutto Resource Center Food Pantry
records.description_en: Free groceries including canned food, fresh produce, frozen items, meat, and hygiene products. Diapers and baby items are available on request when in stock.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who live in Hutto or the Hutto ISD attendance zone. There are no income requirements.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Hutto or Hutto ISD attendance zone

records.how_to_apply: Call (512) 688-0162 before your first visit or register online. You will get an emailed barcode to bring to your first distribution.
records.hours: Saturday drive-thru: 1st, 3rd, and 5th Saturday, 9 AM-12 PM. Wednesday pop-up (fresh/frozen): every Wednesday, 2-3:30 PM.
records.notes: Also offers Golden Connections home deliveries and wellness checks for seniors.

records.name: Hutto Resource Center Financial Assistance
records.description_en: Helps pay utility bills (gas, water, electric, trash), utility connection, medicine, doctor visits, medical bills, and some medical equipment. It does not pay rent or housing costs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who live in Hutto or the Hutto ISD attendance zone. Help is considered once every 12 months for returning clients.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Hutto or Hutto ISD attendance zone

records.how_to_apply: Apply with the online form on the website, or call (512) 688-0162 for help.
records.notes: Amount depends on available funding. Required documents are not listed online - call to ask.

records.name: Hill Country Community Ministries Food Pantry and Assistance
records.description_en: Food pantry, Community Cupboard, Fresh Food For All produce distribution, and other emergency help for families in the Leander and Cedar Park area.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the Leander/Cedar Park area. A Leander ISD resource list says the pantry serves ZIP codes 78613, 78641, 78642, 78645, 78717, 78726, 78729, 78732, 78750, and 78759.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the office at 1005 Lacy Drive during open hours to get started, or call (512) 259-0360.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 9 AM-12 PM and 1-3 PM; Thursday extended until 7 PM. Community Cupboard closes 10 minutes before the pantry.
records.notes: ZIP code list comes from the Round Rock ISD Social Work community resource page. Leander ISD notes HCCM may also help with rent or deposits.

records.name: Brighter Days Food Pantry
records.description_en: Church food pantry that also has a clothes closet and senior programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to community members who need food. Eligibility rules were not listed.
records.how_to_apply: Go during pantry hours or call (512) 259-4673 first.
records.hours: Wednesday 5:30-7 PM
records.notes: Listed on the Leander ISD community resources page; could not confirm on the church's own site. Call before visiting.

records.name: Operation Liberty Hill Food Pantry
records.description_en: Community food pantry serving the Liberty Hill and Leander area.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Eligibility rules were not listed; call to ask.
records.how_to_apply: Call (512) 778-5077 or visit during pantry hours.
records.hours: Tue 9 AM-5 PM, Thu 12-6 PM, Fri 12-1 PM
records.notes: Listed on the Leander ISD community resources page; not confirmed on the organization's own site. Call first.

records.name: St. Vincent de Paul Utility and Rent Assistance (Round Rock)
records.organization: Society of St. Vincent de Paul
records.description_en: Helps with utility bills and rent when funds are available.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in need in the Round Rock area. Exact rules were not listed.
records.how_to_apply: Call (512) 255-2330 to ask about help.
records.notes: Listed by the Round Rock ISD Social Work team. Address is the St. William Catholic Church campus. Call to confirm current availability.

records.name: Community Energy Assistance Program (CEAP)
records.organization: Opportunities for Williamson and Burnet Counties (OWBC)
records.description_en: Helps qualifying households pay electric, gas, and propane bills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Williamson and Burnet County residents with income at or below the program's Federal Poverty Level guidelines. At least one household member must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident, and the applicant must be the account holder or an authorized user.
documents_needed: Proof of income for the last 30 days for everyone 18+
Current utility bill(s)
Photo ID and proof of citizenship or legal residence (SAVE form)
SNAP award letter (if you have one)
Signed utility release form (Atmos and City of Austin customers)
records.how_to_apply: Download the application (English or Spanish) from the OWBC website, fill it out, and send it in with your documents. Email utilities@owbc-tx.org or call (512) 763-1400 with questions.
records.notes: Processing can take up to 90 days, so apply before a shutoff if possible. Also offers a self-sufficiency program.

records.name: Head Start / Early Head Start (Williamson County)
records.organization: Opportunities for Williamson and Burnet Counties (OWBC)
records.description_en: Free early learning program for young children from low-income families, with meals included. Runs from August to late June or early July.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For children ages 0-5 from low-income families.
records.how_to_apply: Turn in a paper application (English or Spanish) at any center or at the main office at 604 High Tech Drive, Georgetown, or email the enrollment coordinator.
records.notes: Williamson County centers: Bartlett (254) 527-4645, Florence (254) 793-9495, Harris Ross/Taylor (512) 365-1070, Hutto (512) 642-3144, Leander (512) 570-0480, Mary Bailey/Georgetown (512) 863-5259, Rawleigh Elliott/Georgetown (512) 864-9733, Round Rock (512) 255-4536.

records.name: Round Rock ISD Free and Reduced-Price Meals
records.description_en: Free or reduced-price school breakfast and lunch. Reduced-price meals cost $0. Approval can also lower fees for AP, SAT, ACT, college applications, activities, and some internet service.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Round Rock ISD students whose household income or benefits meet federal school meal rules.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online any time during the school year; it takes about 5 minutes. Benefits can start within 72 hours. You must apply again each school year.
records.notes: Round Rock ISD covers parts of Williamson and Travis counties. The application is confidential. Full prices shown on the site: elementary lunch $3.20, secondary lunch $3.45, breakfast $1.70.

records.name: Families in Transition (FiT) / McKinney-Vento Homeless Education Program
records.organization: Round Rock ISD State & Federal Programs
records.description_en: Helps students who have no stable home enroll right away, stay in their school, get rides to school, and get school supplies, clothing, and referrals to community help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Round Rock ISD students living in a shelter, motel, car, park, or campground, or doubled-up with others because they lost housing or cannot afford it.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the FiT Student Residency Questionnaire online and a staff member will contact you. You can also call the McKinney-Vento/Foster Care liaison at (512) 464-5185.
records.notes: Students can enroll even without school records, immunization records, or a birth certificate. Brochures are available in English and Spanish. Texas homeless education support center: (800) 446-3142.

records.name: The Clothes Closet (Round Rock ISD Council of PTAs)
records.organization: Round Rock ISD Council of PTAs
records.description_en: Free gently used clothing plus new socks and underwear for students, sizes 4T to 2XL.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Any Round Rock ISD student who needs clothing.
records.how_to_apply: Visit a Clothes Closet location during open hours, or ask your school nurse or counselor. Email clothescloset@rrisdpta.org with questions.
records.hours: Voigt Elementary: Wed and Thu 9:30-11:30 AM during the school year, plus 1st Saturday of each month 10 AM-noon. Anderson Mill Elementary (10610 Salt Mill Hollow, Austin): Tue 10 AM-noon, plus 1st Wednesday of each month 5-7 PM.
records.notes: Closed on school holidays. Shoes, backpacks, and infant clothes are not carried.

records.name: Round Rock ISD Free Pre-K
records.description_en: Free or reduced-tuition pre-kindergarten for 3- and 4-year-olds who qualify.
records.eligibility_summary_en: The child must be 4 by September 1 (or 3 if a 3-year-old class is offered) and meet one rule, such as: qualifies for free/reduced school meals, is learning English, is homeless, has been in foster care, or has a parent in the military or who is a qualifying first responder.
records.how_to_apply: Register through Round Rock ISD's Pre-K enrollment pages and show that your child meets one eligibility rule.
records.notes: Children of district classroom teachers are also eligible.

records.name: Georgetown ISD Free and Reduced Meal Application
records.description_en: Free or reduced-price school meals for Georgetown ISD students.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Georgetown ISD families whose income or benefits meet federal school meal rules.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through Skyward Family Access (Online Free and Reduced Meal Application), or contact Georgetown ISD Nutrition Services.
records.notes: Phone and address are the Georgetown ISD main office. Georgetown ISD also has a Homeless and Foster Programs office under Federal Programs.

records.name: Leander ISD Free and Reduced Meal Benefits
records.description_en: Free or reduced-price school meals for Leander ISD students. Students on free/reduced meals can also get a free district laptop rental (mLISD).
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Leander ISD families whose income or benefits meet federal school meal rules.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at My School Apps, or get a paper form at any campus or the Child Nutrition Services office.
records.notes: Leander ISD also offers a weekend Backpack food program through school counselors.

records.name: Leander ISD Homeless (McKinney-Vento) Services and Family Supports
records.description_en: Help for students without a stable home, including enrollment help and support services. The district also lists a PTA clothes closet, Parents as Teachers (birth to 5), and Young Parent Services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Leander ISD students who lack a fixed, regular, adequate place to sleep at night.
records.how_to_apply: Call the District Homeless Liaison at (512) 570-5931 or the Homeless Liaison Assistant at (512) 570-0364.
records.notes: Parents as Teachers: (512) 570-0320. Young Parent Services: (512) 570-0338. Weekend Backpack meals through school counselors.

records.name: Hutto ISD Free and Reduced-Price Meals
records.description_en: Free or reduced-price school meals for Hutto ISD students. The site says all Hutto ISD students get free breakfast in the 2025-2026 school year.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Hutto ISD families whose income or benefits meet federal school meal rules.
documents_needed: Student's first and last name and date of birth (to link your account)
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through SchoolCafe, or get a paper form at the Child Nutrition Services office, 305 E. Live Oak Street, Hutto.
records.notes: SchoolCafe support: (855) 729-2328. Applications usually open in July.

records.name: Pflugerville ISD Social Work and Free/Reduced Meals
records.description_en: District social workers connect families to mental health crisis help, therapy partners, local food help, holiday help, and other community resources. Families can also apply for free or reduced school meals.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Pflugerville ISD students and families.
records.how_to_apply: Contact your campus counselor or the Social Work team through the district website. Apply for meals on the Free and Reduced Meals Application page.
records.notes: Phone is the district main line. Pflugerville ISD is mostly in Travis County with parts in Williamson County. Also runs Project Hope.

records.name: WIC - Round Rock Clinic
records.organization: Williamson County and Cities Health District (WCCHD)
records.description_en: WIC gives monthly healthy foods, nutrition education, and breastfeeding help and support, plus referrals to other services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant women, breastfeeding women with a baby under 1, women who had a baby in the last 6 months, and caregivers of children under 5 who meet income rules. Having a job or private insurance does not disqualify you.
documents_needed: Proof of household income (pay stubs, tax return, or employer statement)
Proof of address (utility bill or rent receipt; no PO boxes)
Photo ID
Proof of Medicaid, TANF, or SNAP if you have it (can replace income proof)
records.how_to_apply: Call the clinic to make an appointment. At the visit you will have a health screening and nutrition check.
records.hours: See the WCCHD calendar for clinic hours
records.notes: Email: RoundRockWIC@wilco.org.

records.how_to_apply: Call the clinic to make an appointment. At the visit you will have a health screening and nutrition check.
records.hours: See the WCCHD calendar for clinic hours. Liberty Hill WIC (155 Hillcrest Lane, appointment only) is open 2nd Wednesday and 4th Monday, 9 AM-5 PM, closed 12-1 PM; call the same number.
records.notes: Email: GeorgetownWIC@wilco.org.

records.name: WilCo Care Indigent Health Program and Healthcare Helpline
records.organization: Williamson County and Cities Health District (WCCHD)
records.description_en: The Healthcare Helpline helps residents find and apply for health programs. WilCo Care pays for needed medical care for very low-income adults, including doctor visits, hospital care, emergency care, up to 3 medicines a month, glasses, and mental health care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: WilCo Care is for Williamson County residents age 18+ with income below 21% of the Federal Poverty Level who cannot get Medicaid. The Helpline is open to any county resident.
documents_needed: Valid Social Security card
Proof of income
Proof of Williamson County residency
records.how_to_apply: Call the Healthcare Helpline at (512) 248-3252 or visit 355 Texas Ave, Round Rock, Mon-Fri 8 AM-5 PM.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 8 AM-5 PM
records.notes: Yearly benefit limit is $30,000 per person; hospital care up to 30 days/$30,000. Resource (asset) limits under Texas Health & Safety Code Ch. 61 also apply.

records.name: WCCHD Immunization Clinics (Vaccines for Children and Adult Safety Net)
records.organization: Williamson County and Cities Health District (WCCHD)
records.description_en: Low-cost shots for children and uninsured adults at public health centers in Round Rock, Cedar Park, and Taylor. Flu shots are free for everyone 6 months and older.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Child vaccines: ages birth-18 with Medicaid, CHIP, no insurance, or not enough insurance, or American Indian/Alaska Native. Adult vaccines: only adults with no health insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call Clinical Services at (512) 943-3600 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Low cost (administration fees may apply); flu shots free
records.notes: Other public health centers: Cedar Park, 350 Discovery Blvd #102, (512) 260-4240; Taylor, 115 W 6th St, (512) 238-2121. Travel vaccines are not offered.

records.name: Lone Star Circle of Care - Texas A&M Health Science Center (Round Rock)
records.description_en: Community health center offering family medicine, pediatrics, senior health, women's health, behavioral health, pharmacy, and specialty care. Patients with or without insurance are seen.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, insured or uninsured. Accepts Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare, and many private plans; staff can help uninsured patients make care affordable.
records.how_to_apply: Call (877) 800-5722 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Sliding scale for uninsured; insurance accepted
records.notes: Free help signing up for Marketplace insurance, Medicaid, or CHIP: Patient Services (512) 686-0534.

records.description_en: Community health center offering pediatrics, dental, and behavioral health care. Patients with or without insurance are seen.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, insured or uninsured. Accepts Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare, and many private plans; staff can help uninsured patients make care affordable.
records.how_to_apply: Call (877) 800-5722 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Sliding scale for uninsured; insurance accepted
records.notes: Round Rock ISD lists this as the pediatrics site (sports physicals, well-child visits) and says it accepts Medicaid, Medicare, WilCo, and offers a sliding scale for uninsured. Behavioral health requires first seeing an LSCC primary care provider.

records.description_en: Community health center offering school-linked primary care. Patients with or without insurance are seen.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, insured or uninsured. Accepts Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare, and many private plans; staff can help uninsured patients make care affordable.
records.how_to_apply: Call (877) 800-5722 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Sliding scale for uninsured; insurance accepted
records.notes: Run by Lone Star Circle of Care with Georgetown ISD. Call (512) 688-6250 to ask who can be seen and hours.

records.name: Sacred Heart Community Clinic
records.description_en: Free primary care, dental care, lab work, and diabetes education for adults without insurance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For uninsured adults in Williamson County.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the New Patient Packet on the website, then register during registration hours or call (512) 716-3929.
records.hours: Mon 8 AM-3 PM; Tue 8 AM-5 PM; Wed closed; Thu 10 AM-4 PM; Fri 8 AM-12 PM (registration hours differ)
records.notes: Located at the back of the St. William Church campus.

records.name: Bluebonnet Trails Community Services (Mental Health, IDD, Substance Use)
records.description_en: The public mental health and disability center for Williamson County. It offers mental health care, a 24/7 crisis line, substance use treatment, autism and disability (IDD) services, veteran and peer support, supportive housing, and job help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For children and adults in its Central Texas service area who need mental health, substance use, or disability services.
records.how_to_apply: Call (844) 309-6385 (7:30 AM-5:30 PM) to start services. In a crisis, call the 24/7 crisis line at (800) 841-1255.
records.hours: Main line 7:30 AM-5:30 PM; crisis line 24/7
records.notes: Other Williamson County sites: Cedar Park (1401 Medical Pkwy, Bldg C, Suite 300), Taylor (1301 W 4th St), Liberty Hill (155 Hillcrest Ln). 24/7 crisis line: (800) 841-1255.

records.name: Early Childhood Intervention (ECI)
records.description_en: Services for babies and toddlers who have delays or disabilities, to help them grow and learn.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For children from birth to age 3 with developmental delays or disabilities.
records.how_to_apply: Call Bluebonnet Trails at (844) 309-6385 to ask for an ECI screening.
records.notes: Bluebonnet Trails also runs autism services for ages 3-15 and Parents as Teachers.

records.name: Williamson County Mobile Outreach Team (MOT)
records.description_en: Trained team that responds to mental health crisis calls in the community.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For anyone in Williamson County having a mental health crisis. If there is immediate danger, call 911. You can also call or text 988.
records.how_to_apply: Call (512) 864-8277. In an emergency call 911.
records.notes: Listed by the Round Rock ISD Social Work team; not confirmed on a Williamson County page this session.

records.name: Hope Alliance Family Violence and Sexual Assault Services
records.description_en: Free, private help for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault: 24-hour hotline, emergency shelter at a safe location, counseling for adults and children, housing help, and legal advocacy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Williamson County affected by family violence or sexual assault.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour hotline at (800) 460-7233. For non-urgent needs call the office at (512) 255-1212.
records.hours: Hotline 24/7. Crisis chat: Mon-Thu 12-4 PM and Mon-Fri 5-10 PM.
records.notes: Shelter location is confidential. The contact form is not checked daily - use the hotline for urgent needs.

records.name: STARRY Free Family Counseling
records.description_en: Free counseling for kids and families, including individual, group, and family counseling and parenting classes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For children ages 6-17 and their families. Insurance and income are not a barrier.
records.how_to_apply: Register through STARRY's client portal or call the nearest office.
records.notes: Phone number comes from the Round Rock ISD community resource list. STARRY lists a Williamson County office and a Liberty Hill Family Resource Center.

records.name: Round Rock Police Victim Assistance
records.description_en: Helps crime victims with crisis support, court accompaniment, information about their rights, case updates, and referrals for housing, medical care, food, and money.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For victims of crimes such as assault, sexual assault, kidnapping, or robbery, and close relatives of victims who died.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Victim Assistance Coordinator at (512) 341-3124.
records.hours: Staff on call 24/7

records.name: Georgetown Housing Authority (Section 8 and Public Housing)
records.description_en: Runs the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program and affordable apartments (Stonehaven and Shady Oaks) in Georgetown, with services for older and disabled residents.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households; program rules apply.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Section 8 office at (512) 869-6918 or see the application page on the website.
records.notes: Stonehaven Apartments: 210 W 18th St, (512) 863-5565. Shady Oaks Apartments: 501 E. Janis Dr., (512) 863-2522. Waitlist status not shown - call.

records.name: Taylor Housing Authority (Section 8)
records.description_en: Runs the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program for about 250 families in Taylor.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households. The Section 8 waitlist is currently closed.
records.how_to_apply: Watch the website for waitlist openings, which happen every few years.
records.notes: Waitlist CLOSED as of this check. No longer offers public housing (since Dec 23, 2025). No emergency housing available.

records.name: Allen R. Baca Center for Senior and Community Activities
records.organization: City of Round Rock Parks and Recreation
records.description_en: Senior center with low-cost lunches for people 60+ (through OWBC), fitness, classes, social clubs, and day trips.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Programs are for adults 50+. The OWBC lunch program is for seniors 60+.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the center or call (512) 218-5499 to join. For lunch, come Mon-Fri at noon.
records.hours: Office Mon-Fri 7:30 AM-5:30 PM. Lunch Mon-Fri 12-12:30 PM.

records.name: Williamson County Veteran Services Office
records.description_en: Helps veterans and families apply for VA, Texas, and county benefits. It also offers one-time emergency financial help through a Texas Veterans Commission grant.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For veterans, current and surviving spouses, and dependent children who live in Williamson County.
records.how_to_apply: Call (512) 943-1900 to make an appointment. Emergency financial help can be requested with the online form.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 8 AM-5 PM, by appointment only
records.notes: Service officers also work at annexes in Round Rock (Hallie Jester Annex) and Taylor.

records.name: CARTS Rural and Interurban Transit
records.description_en: Bus and on-demand rides in rural Williamson County and between towns. Seniors 60+, people with disabilities, and kids under 12 pay half fare.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public. Half fare for seniors 60+, people with disabilities, and children under 12. Seniors 60+ ride free on Country Bus routes.
records.how_to_apply: Book online or call the Reservations Center at (512) 478-7433. Buy passes in the Token Transit app.
records.cost: $2-$6 depending on zone; 50% off for reduced-fare riders
records.notes: Main office: (512) 481-1011. Drivers cannot make change.

records.name: Round Rock Rides On-Demand and ADA Paratransit
records.description_en: On-demand shared rides inside Round Rock city limits, plus curb-to-curb paratransit for people with disabilities who qualify.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone can ride. Reduced fare for seniors 65+, eligible paratransit riders, and active-duty military. Paratransit needs an application and assessment.
records.how_to_apply: Book in the app, at book.roundrock.rideco.com, or call (512) 312-2124. For paratransit eligibility call (737) 610-5384.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 6 AM-8 PM; Sat 8 AM-6 PM; closed Sunday
records.cost: $4 one-way; $2 reduced fare; paratransit $2 per trip
records.notes: CapMetro routes 50, 152, and 980 also serve Round Rock. Book 30 minutes to 7 days ahead.

records.name: GoGeo Paratransit (Georgetown)
records.description_en: Curb-to-curb rides for people with disabilities who live in Georgetown city limits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For qualified people with disabilities living in Georgetown city limits.
records.how_to_apply: Reserve at least 24 hours ahead by phone at (512) 478-7433 or online.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 7 AM-7 PM

records.name: CapMetro Equifare and Reduced Fare
records.description_en: Lower bus and train fares for low-income riders (Equifare), and reduced fares for seniors, Medicare card holders, riders with disabilities, and military.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Equifare: household income below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level, or enrolled in a social services program. Reduced Fare: age 65+, Medicare card, disability, or military ID.
documents_needed: Proof such as a Medicaid card, EBT card, Social Security award letter, recent pay stub, or tax return (self-verification allowed)
records.how_to_apply: Apply online in about 15 minutes, or get a paper form at the Transit Store, 1705 Guadalupe St., Austin. Approval takes 4-6 business days.
records.cost: Equifare local: $1 ride / $33 month. Reduced local: $0.60 ride / $20.60 month
records.notes: Must use a CapMetro Reloadable Fare Card or the Umo app. Serves Round Rock routes and Leander in Williamson County.

records.name: Workforce Solutions of Williamson (Round Rock)
records.description_en: Free job search help, training programs, and child care financial help (Child Care Services) for working parents.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job services are open to anyone. Child care help has income and work/school rules.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the center or call (512) 244-2207.
records.address: 575 Round Rock West Drive, Building H, Suite 240
records.notes: Main regional line: (844) 344-2780.

records.name: Workforce Solutions of Taylor
records.description_en: Free job search help, training, and child care help referrals in eastern Williamson County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to job seekers. Child care help has income and work/school rules.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the center or call (512) 580-4274.

records.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid (TRLA)
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as housing, family, and benefits problems.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income people in TRLA's 68-county service area, which includes Williamson and Travis counties.
records.how_to_apply: Call the intake line at (833) 329-8752 (toll-free) or (956) 996-8752, weekdays 9 AM-5 PM Central.
records.hours: Intake phone: weekdays 9 AM-5 PM
records.notes: Austin office listed; intake is by phone.

records.name: Round Rock Public Library - Free Computers, Wi-Fi, ESL and Job Help
records.description_en: Free public computers and Wi-Fi, laptop lending, English (ESL) classes, adult education, and career help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone. Guests without a library card can use computers with a guest pass. Borrowing a laptop needs a library card and Texas ID.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the library. Ask at the desk for a guest pass or a library card.
records.hours: Mon-Thu 9 AM-9 PM; Fri-Sat 9 AM-6 PM; Sun 1-6 PM

records.name: Georgetown Public Library - Free Computers and Wi-Fi
records.description_en: Free public computers and Wi-Fi, study rooms, and digital resources.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the library, call (512) 930-3551, or text (512) 686-7247.
records.hours: Mon-Thu 9 AM-8 PM; Fri 9 AM-6 PM; Sat 9 AM-5 PM; Sun 12-5 PM
